subject: Physics
question: Which of the following elements is ferromagnetic and strongly attracted by a permanent magnet?

options.A: Iron (and Cobalt, Nickel)
options.B: Copper
options.C: Aluminum

explanation: Iron, cobalt, and nickel have magnetic domains that align strongly with external magnetic fields, making them ferromagnetic.

subject: Physics
question: Outside a permanent bar magnet, the magnetic field lines always emerge from the:

options.A: North pole and enter the South pole
options.B: South pole and enter the North pole
options.C: Center toward both poles

explanation: By convention, external magnetic field lines travel from the North pole to the South pole, forming continuous closed loops.

subject: Physics
question: Why can two magnetic field lines NEVER intersect or cross each other?

options.A: A compass needle at the point of intersection cannot point in two different directions at the same instant
options.B: Magnetic lines are electrostatic charges that repel
options.C: Field lines have infinite thickness

explanation: If field lines crossed, the resultant magnetic field at the intersection would have two directions simultaneously, which is impossible.

subject: Physics
question: The magnetic field strength of an electromagnet (solenoid) can be increased by:

options.A: Increasing the current and increasing the number of turns in the coil
options.B: Decreasing the number of turns and reducing current
options.C: Using a plastic core instead of soft iron

explanation: Magnetic field $B \propto n I$, so increasing current ($I$), increasing turns per unit length ($n$), or adding a soft iron core boosts electromagnet strength.

subject: Physics
question: Sensitive electronic instruments and mechanical watches are shielded from external stray magnetic fields by enclosing them in a box made of:

options.A: Soft iron
options.B: Copper
options.C: Aluminum

explanation: Soft iron has high magnetic permeability, channeling external field lines through its walls and shielding the interior cavity.

subject: Physics
question: A permanent magnet can be demagnetized most effectively by:

options.A: Heating it to a high temperature (Curie point) or hammering it while aligned East-West
options.B: Cooling it to freezing temperatures
options.C: Placing it in a vacuum

explanation: Heating or mechanical hammering agitates magnetic domains, destroying their alignment and demagnetizing the material.

subject: Physics
question: Soft iron is used for making temporary electromagnet cores rather than steel because soft iron:

options.A: Magnetizes easily and loses its magnetism rapidly when current is switched off (low retentivity)
options.B: Retains its magnetism permanently forever
options.C: Has higher electrical resistance than steel

explanation: Soft iron has high magnetic permeability and low retentivity, demagnetizing immediately when the magnetizing current ceases.

subject: Physics
question: When viewing the end of a solenoid carrying an electric current, if the current flows in a CLOCKWISE direction, that end acts as a:

options.A: South magnetic pole
options.B: North magnetic pole
options.C: Neutral pole

explanation: By the Clock Rule (right-hand rule), a clockwise current loop generates a South magnetic pole facing the observer.

subject: Physics
question: If a permanent bar magnet with North and South poles is broken into two equal halves:

options.A: Each broken piece becomes a complete magnet having both North and South poles
options.B: One piece becomes an isolated North pole and the other an isolated South pole
options.C: Both pieces lose their magnetism completely
options.D: The pieces attract each other only at the break point

explanation: Isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist; breaking a magnet produces two smaller complete dipole magnets.

subject: Physics
question: In an electric bell mechanism, when the striker hits the gong, the electrical circuit is broken at the:

options.A: Contact adjustment screw
options.B: Battery terminal
options.C: Electromagnet coil

explanation: The movement of the soft iron armature pulls it away from the contact screw, opening the circuit, demagnetizing the core, and allowing the spring to reset the armature.

subject: Physics
question: According to the domain theory of magnetism, in an unmagnetized piece of iron:

options.A: Magnetic domains are randomly oriented, so their magnetic fields cancel each other out
options.B: All magnetic domains point in the same direction
options.C: Atoms possess zero net spin or magnetic dipole moments
options.D: All electrons have escaped from the iron lattice

explanation: In an unmagnetized iron bar, individual microscopic domains (clusters of aligned dipoles) point in random directions, producing a net zero external magnetic field.

subject: Physics
question: When grasping a straight current-carrying conductor with the right hand so the thumb points in the direction of conventional electric current, the curled fingers indicate:

options.A: The direction of the circular magnetic field lines around the wire
options.B: The direction of electrostatic force
options.C: The direction of electron drift

explanation: By the Right-Hand Grip Rule, the curled fingers encircle the wire in the direction of the concentric magnetic field lines.

subject: Physics
question: Soft iron pieces called "magnetic keepers" are placed across the ends of bar magnets during storage in order to:

options.A: Form closed continuous magnetic loops and prevent self-demagnetization from free poles
options.B: Make the magnets lighter in weight
options.C: Conduct electric current through the magnets

explanation: Unshielded end poles produce demagnetizing fields. Soft iron keepers complete closed magnetic loops, preserving domain alignment indefinitely.

subject: Physics
question: A freely suspended magnetic needle aligns itself approximately in the North-South direction because:

options.A: Earth acts like a giant bar magnet with its magnetic South pole situated near the geographic North pole
options.B: Earth rotates from East to West
options.C: The Sun pulls the North pole with solar gravity
options.D: Atmospheric pressure pushes the needle North

explanation: The North-seeking pole of a compass is attracted towards Earth's northern geographic region because the magnetic South pole of Earth resides near the geographic North pole.

subject: Physics
question: The temporary magnetization of a soft iron nail when brought close to or in contact with a permanent magnet is known as:

options.A: Magnetic induction
options.B: Electromagnetic radiation
options.C: Electrostatic friction

explanation: Magnetic induction is the process by which an unmagnetized magnetic material acquires magnetic properties when placed within a magnetic field.

subject: Physics
question: The magnetic field inside a long, tightly wound current-carrying solenoid is:

options.A: Uniform and parallel along the axis of the solenoid
options.B: Zero everywhere inside
options.C: Strongest at the outer surface and zero at the center

explanation: Inside a long solenoid, magnetic field lines are straight, parallel, and evenly spaced, indicating a uniform and strong magnetic field.

subject: Physics
question: An electromagnetic relay switch is an electrical device designed to:

options.A: Control a high-voltage, high-current circuit safely using a low-voltage, low-current control signal
options.B: Store permanent electrostatic charges
options.C: Convert alternating current into direct current
options.D: Generate mechanical power like an engine

explanation: An electromagnetic relay uses a small current in an electromagnet coil to attract an armature, closing contacts in a separate high-power circuit.

subject: Physics
question: A steel needle can be magnetized most strongly and uniformly by:

options.A: Placing it inside a solenoid carrying a direct current (DC)
options.B: Placing it inside a coil carrying alternating current (AC)
options.C: Heating it red hot in a furnace

explanation: Direct current in a solenoid establishes a strong, steady, unidirectional magnetic field that permanently aligns magnetic domains in steel.

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following substances is completely non-magnetic and cannot be magnetized or attracted by a magnet?

options.A: Copper (as well as Brass, Wood, and Glass)
options.B: Steel
options.C: Nickel

explanation: Copper, brass, aluminum, wood, and glass are non-magnetic materials with no net ferromagnetism and are unaffected by ordinary magnetic fields.

subject: Physics
question: Magnetic levitation (Maglev) bullet trains achieve ultra-high speeds with minimal friction because:

options.A: Electromagnets produce magnetic repulsion that lifts the train above the guideway track, eliminating mechanical rolling friction
options.B: Trains run in a vacuum tube without motors
options.C: Permanent magnets pull the train using gravitational force
options.D: Air resistance is converted into electricity

explanation: Maglev trains employ magnetic repulsion between onboard superconducting magnets and track coils to hover 10–15 mm above the track, eliminating surface friction.

subject: Physics
question: The fundamental law of magnetic poles states that:

options.A: Like magnetic poles repel each other, and unlike magnetic poles attract each other
options.B: Like magnetic poles attract each other
options.C: All magnetic poles attract unmagnetized aluminum
options.D: North poles attract North poles with double force

explanation: Fundamental law of magnetism: Like poles (N-N, S-S) repel, whereas unlike poles (N-S) attract.

subject: Physics
question: The only definitive and sure experimental test to verify whether a metallic bar is permanently magnetized is:

options.A: Repulsion by a known magnetic pole of a compass needle
options.B: Attraction to an iron nail
options.C: Attraction to a steel rod

explanation: Unmagnetized magnetic materials (like soft iron) are attracted by both poles of a magnet. Only a magnetized body will experience repulsion when presented with a like pole.

subject: Physics
question: Geographically, near the Earth’s northern geographic pole lies the Earth’s:

options.A: Magnetic South Pole
options.B: Magnetic North Pole
options.C: Magnetic Equator

explanation: Because unlike poles attract, the North-seeking pole of a compass points north towards the Earth’s geographic North pole, meaning a magnetic South pole is situated there.

subject: Physics
question: The vertical angle that the total Earth's magnetic field vector makes with the horizontal plane at any location on Earth is termed the:

options.A: Angle of Dip (Magnetic Inclination)
options.B: Angle of Declination
options.C: Magnetic Latitude

explanation: The Angle of Dip (or Magnetic Inclination) is the angle between the Earth’s magnetic field lines and the horizontal surface.

subject: Physics
question: Steel is chosen over soft iron for manufacturing permanent bar magnets because steel exhibits:

options.A: High coercivity (strong resistance to demagnetization)
options.B: Zero magnetic retentivity
options.C: Ease of demagnetization with gentle tapping

explanation: Steel has high magnetic retentivity and high coercivity, making it difficult to magnetize but once magnetized, it retains its magnetism permanently.

subject: Physics
question: At the exact geometric center of a flat circular current-carrying coil, the magnetic field lines are:

options.A: Straight and perpendicular to the plane of the coil
options.B: Concentric circles parallel to the coil plane
options.C: Zero in magnitude

explanation: At the center of a circular current loop, the magnetic field contributions from all wire segments combine into straight, parallel field lines perpendicular to the loop’s plane.

subject: Physics
question: The critical temperature above which a ferromagnetic substance loses its permanent ferromagnetism and behaves as a paramagnetic material is called the:

options.A: Curie Temperature
options.B: Absolute Zero
options.C: Inversion Temperature

explanation: At the Curie temperature, thermal kinetic agitation destroys the alignment of magnetic domains in ferromagnetic substances (e.g., $770^\circ\text{C}$ for iron).

subject: Physics
question: When using the Right-Hand Grip Rule for a solenoid, if the curled fingers point in the direction of conventional electric current, the extended thumb points towards the:

options.A: Magnetic North Pole of the solenoid
options.B: Magnetic South Pole of the solenoid
options.C: Direction of electron flow

explanation: By the Right-Hand Grip Rule for coils and solenoids, the thumb points in the direction of the internal magnetic field, which is toward the magnetic North pole.

subject: Physics
question: The lifting force of an industrial electromagnet used in scrapyards can be effectively increased by:

options.A: Increasing the electric current and the number of turns in the coil
options.B: Decreasing the number of turns of wire
options.C: Replacing the soft iron core with a plastic core

explanation: Magnetic field strength $B \propto n I$. Increasing the number of turns per unit length ($n$) and current ($I$) directly strengthens the electromagnet.

subject: Physics
question: Materials like copper, bismuth, and water that are feebly repelled by strong magnetic fields are classified as:

options.A: Diamagnetic materials
options.B: Paramagnetic materials
options.C: Ferromagnetic materials

explanation: Diamagnetic substances are weakly repelled by magnets because an applied magnetic field induces a weak opposing magnetic moment in their atomic orbitals.

subject: Physics
question: Hans Christian Oersted experimentally discovered that an electric current creates a magnetic field when he observed that:

options.A: A nearby magnetic compass needle deflected whenever an electric current passed through a nearby wire
options.B: An electric charge was created on a dry glass rod
options.C: A bar magnet fell faster through an empty glass tube
options.D: Iron filings melted when touched with a wire

explanation: In 1820, Oersted discovered electromagnetism by noticing that a current-carrying wire deflected a nearby magnetic compass needle, proving that electric currents produce surrounding magnetic fields.

subject: Physics
question: The angle of dip (or magnetic inclination) made by the Earth’s total magnetic field vector with the horizontal plane at the Earth’s magnetic equator is:

options.A: $0^\circ$
options.B: $90^\circ$
options.C: $45^\circ$

explanation: At the Earth's magnetic equator, the Earth’s magnetic field lines are parallel to the horizontal surface, so the angle of dip is $0^\circ$. At the magnetic poles, the field lines are vertical (dip $= 90^\circ$).

subject: Physics
question: A permanent bar magnet can be demagnetized effectively using an electrical method by:

options.A: Placing it inside a solenoid connected to an alternating current (AC) source oriented East-West and slowly withdrawing it
options.B: Connecting both ends of the magnet directly to a direct current (DC) battery
options.C: Submerging the magnet in ice-cold salt water
options.D: Wrapping the magnet in plastic insulation

explanation: Alternating current (AC) reverses magnetic field direction rapidly. Slowly withdrawing the magnet while the AC field decays leaves the magnetic domains randomly oriented, resulting in complete demagnetization.

subject: Physics
question: In the magnetic field mapping around a permanent bar magnet placed on a table, "Neutral Points" are specific points where:

options.A: The magnetic field of the bar magnet is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the Earth’s horizontal magnetic field, resulting in a net magnetic field of zero
options.B: The magnetic field strength reaches its absolute maximum value
options.C: A compass needle spins continuously at high speed
options.D: Magnetic field lines cross and intersect each other

explanation: Neutral points are locations where the magnet’s magnetic field exactly cancels out the Earth’s horizontal magnetic field ($B_{\text{magnet}} = B_{\text{Earth}}$ in opposite directions), so the net magnetic field is zero.

subject: Physics
question: When the North pole of a permanent bar magnet is brought close to (without touching) one end of an unmagnetized soft iron bar, the nearer end of the iron bar acquires an:

options.A: Induced South pole (and is attracted)
options.B: Induced North pole (and is repelled)
options.C: Permanent North pole

explanation: By magnetic induction, magnetic domains in the soft iron align so that an opposite pole (South pole) is induced at the nearer end, creating an attractive magnetic force.

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following alloys is categorized as a "hard magnetic material" suitable for manufacturing strong, long-lasting permanent magnets?

options.A: Alnico (alloy of aluminum, nickel, and cobalt)
options.B: Soft annealed iron
options.C: Pure electrolytic copper

explanation: Alnico, steel, and neodymium alloys are magnetically hard materials with high retentivity and coercivity, retaining strong magnetization permanently.

subject: Physics
question: The pattern of magnetic field lines produced around a long, straight conductor carrying a steady electric current consists of:

options.A: Concentric circles centered on the wire axis in planes perpendicular to the wire
options.B: Straight parallel lines radiating outwards away from the wire
options.C: Helical spirals traveling along the length of the wire
options.D: Elliptical loops parallel to the conductor

explanation: The magnetic field of a straight current-carrying wire forms concentric circular field lines centered on the wire, whose direction is determined by the Right-Hand Grip Rule.

subject: Physics
question: In a magnetic field diagram of a permanent bar magnet, as the distance from the magnetic pole increases, the field lines become wider apart, indicating that:

options.A: The magnetic field strength decreases steadily with increasing distance
options.B: The magnetic field becomes uniform and constant
options.C: The polarity of the magnet reverses spontaneously
options.D: The field lines cross one another

explanation: The density/closeness of magnetic field lines is directly proportional to the magnetic field strength. Closer lines near poles represent strong magnetic field; widening lines indicate weakening field strength.

subject: Physics
question: In an electric bell mechanism, the continuous ringing action when the push-button switch is held down occurs because of the:

options.A: Make-and-break contact screw that repeatedly completes and interrupts the electromagnet circuit
options.B: Permanent magnet that rotates continuously
options.C: Thermal expansion of the copper bell gong
options.D: Continuous chemical reaction inside the striker

explanation: When current energizes the electromagnet, it attracts the armature and strikes the gong; this pulls the spring away from the contact screw, breaking the circuit. The spring returns the armature, re-establishing contact in a rapid make-and-break cycle.

subject: Physics
question: Earth’s Magnetic Declination at any geographical location is defined as the angle between the:

options.A: True geographic meridian (True North) and the magnetic meridian (Magnetic North)
options.B: Horizontal magnetic field and the vertical magnetic field component
options.C: Magnetic equator and the geographic equator
options.D: Earth’s rotational axis and the plane of the Moon’s orbit

explanation: Magnetic Declination (or magnetic variation) is the horizontal angle between true geographic North (geographic meridian) and the direction indicated by a magnetic compass (magnetic meridian).

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following materials is a ferromagnetic substance strongly attracted by magnetic fields?

options.A: Cobalt
options.B: Copper
options.C: Aluminum

explanation: Cobalt, Iron, Nickel, and their alloys are ferromagnetic materials with high magnetic permeability that are strongly attracted by magnets.

subject: Physics
question: Why is soft iron preferred over hard steel for the core of electromagnets and electric bells?

options.A: Soft iron is easily magnetized and rapidly loses its magnetism when the current is switched off
options.B: Soft iron becomes a permanent magnet permanently
options.C: Soft iron has zero electrical conductivity
options.D: Soft iron is much harder than steel

explanation: Soft iron is a temporary magnetic material with high permeability and low retentivity/coercivity, allowing it to magnetize instantly when current flows and demagnetize immediately when current stops.

subject: Physics
question: What is the most effective method for completely demagnetizing a permanent steel bar magnet in the laboratory?

options.A: Placing it inside an East-West aligned solenoid carrying AC current and slowly withdrawing it
options.B: Immersing it in cold ice water
options.C: Stroking it repeatedly in one direction with a copper rod
options.D: Connecting it to a direct current (DC) battery

explanation: Alternating current (AC) rapidly reverses magnetic domain orientation. Slowly withdrawing the magnet from an energized AC solenoid oriented East-West leaves magnetic domains randomized, neutralizing net magnetism.

subject: Physics
question: If a bar magnet is cut into two equal halves transversely through its middle, what is the result?

options.A: Two complete smaller magnets, each possessing both a North and a South pole
options.B: One piece with only a North pole and one piece with only a South pole
options.C: Both pieces become completely unmagnetized
options.D: One piece remains magnetic while the other loses magnetism

explanation: Magnetic monopoles do not exist in nature. Cutting a bar magnet produces new opposite poles at the cut faces, creating two complete bipolar magnets.

subject: Physics
question: In the external region surrounding a permanent bar magnet, magnetic field lines are directed from:

options.A: North pole to South pole
options.B: South pole to North pole
options.C: Center of magnet outwards radially in all directions

explanation: By standard scientific convention, external magnetic field lines emerge from the North pole and curve around to enter the South pole, forming continuous closed loops.

subject: Physics
question: How can sensitive electronic circuits and mechanical watches be effectively shielded from external stray magnetic fields?

options.A: Enclosing them in a soft iron magnetic screening casing
options.B: Wrapping them with thick copper foil
options.C: Surrounding them with permanent bar magnets
options.D: Placing them in an airtight plastic vacuum container

explanation: Soft iron has very high magnetic permeability. Magnetic field lines preferentially pass through the soft iron shield walls rather than entering the hollow interior (magnetic screening).

subject: Physics
question: The strength of the magnetic field produced inside a current-carrying solenoid can be enhanced by:

options.A: Inserting a soft iron core and increasing the electric current
options.B: Decreasing the number of coil turns per unit length
options.C: Replacing the copper coil with an insulator
options.D: Increasing the diameter while keeping coil turns constant

explanation: The solenoid field strength is $B = \mu n I$. It is increased by raising current $I$, increasing turn density $n$, and adding a high-permeability soft iron core.

subject: Physics
question: Which magnetic interaction test is considered the ONLY sure, definitive proof that an unknown metallic specimen is magnetized?

options.A: Magnetic repulsion with a known pole of a magnet
options.B: Magnetic attraction to a known pole of a magnet
options.C: Ability to conduct electric current

explanation: An unmagnetized magnetic material (like soft iron) is attracted by both poles of a magnet. Repulsion occurs only between two like magnetic poles, making repulsion the only sure test of magnetization.

subject: Physics
question: What is the geometric shape of magnetic field lines in the plane perpendicular to a long straight current-carrying wire?

options.A: Concentric circles centered on the wire
options.B: Straight parallel lines radiating outwards
options.C: Elliptical loops extending to infinity

explanation: The magnetic field of a straight current-carrying conductor consists of concentric circular lines centered on the wire, whose direction is given by the Right-Hand Grip Rule.

subject: Physics
question: Permanent magnets are manufactured primarily from hard steel or Alnico alloys because these materials possess:

options.A: High magnetic retentivity and high coercivity
options.B: Low magnetic retentivity and zero resistance
options.C: High thermal expansion and low density

explanation: High retentivity ensures strong residual magnetism, while high coercivity resists demagnetization from stray fields, shocks, and temperature variations.
